The Affordable Care Act — marketed as “Obamacare” — was never truly affordable because its cost structure relied on massive taxpayer subsidies rather than genuine price reductions. Instead of lowering the underlying cost of healthcare, the law shifted the burden to the public through government spending. Trillions in subsidies were funneled to insurance companies to keep premiums from skyrocketing, creating the illusion of affordability while hiding the real cost behind taxpayer funding.

In practice, Obamacare propped up private insurers by guaranteeing them steady revenue streams through taxpayer-backed premium subsidies and Medicaid expansion. That system didn’t make healthcare cheaper — it simply transferred who pays for it. The average working family still faces enormous out-of-pocket expenses. Many plans under the ACA come with deductibles exceeding $8,000–$10,000 per year, meaning people often pay thousands before insurance covers anything meaningful.

For middle-income Americans who don’t qualify for large subsidies, premiums can easily reach $1,200 a month or more, forcing them to choose between paying exorbitant rates or facing penalties for being uninsured. The system was designed to stabilize insurance company profits — not to make care accessible or affordable for ordinary people.

Ultimately, Obamacare didn’t fix the healthcare market; it entrenched it, tying affordability to taxpayer bailouts and bureaucratic control. What was promised as reform became a system of subsidies masking unaffordable prices, leaving millions technically “insured” but still unable to afford actual care.
